newsitem.title: USA: Official says no U.S. conclusion on Iran bomb link.
newsitem.headline: Official says no U.S. conclusion on Iran bomb link.

text.p: The United States has not concluded that Iran was behind the deadly truck bombing of a U.S. military housing complex in Saudi Arabia but will take action if it does, a U.S. official said on Thursday.

"This is a matter that is still under investigation. We haven't reached any conclusions yet," Acting Assistant Secretary of State David Welch said at a Senate hearing. "But when we do we will take an appropriate action."
He refused to say what action could be taken but said "We have a variety of tools that we can use in these situations. We're not ruling any of them in or any of them out."

Welch made the comment at a Senate Foreign Relations subcommittee hearing when asked about a Washington Post story saying an Iranian official has been linked to the Saudi truck bombing that killed 19 U.S. servicemen last year.

The newspaper quoted U.S. and Saudi officials as saying Brig. Ahmad Sherifi, a senior Iranian intelligence officer, met two years before the bombing with Hani Abd Rahim Sayegh, a Saudi Shiite arrested in Canada last month as a participant.
The newspaper said U.S. officials disagreed whether the link was strong enough to require U.S. retaliation against Iran.
Sen. Charles Robb, a Virginia Democrat, asked Welch if U.S. bombing of terror camps inside Iran or extension of the Iraq naval embargo to include Iran would be appropriate actions.
But Welch said he could make no comment on what action the United States might take if it concluded Iran was involved in the bombing.
